an3.63:1.1: This village does not seem to be mentioned elsewhere.
an3.63:2.1: This is not the Vacchagotta famed for asking questions ([mn71:2.1]()).
an3.63:3.7: Legend has it that on the slopes of Mount Meru grows the vast Jambu tree that gives the continent of India her name, “the land of the black plum tree”. The fruits of that tree are as big as elephants, and when they fall, their juice flows forth as a river named Jambu. The dried mud of that river yields gold nuggets whose unparalleled lustre is highly sought-after among the gods. This is that gold (Śiva Purāṇa 17.16–19).
an3.63:6.9: _Evaṁbhūta_ (literally, “one who has become thus”) means one who has come to be of such a character, or endowed with such qualities ([an4.11:1.3](), [ja340:4.3](), [ja371:1.1]()). It does not mean “while still in the state of absorption”. It is used in the same way in the Yogic text Amanaska 2.99, where a meditator who has attained enlightenment is said to have “become such”.
